description: Compares the published Toffoli transfer-matrix entries against the only construction the corpus records (_deprecated/toffoli-braid.py). An independent reconstruction reproduces that producer exactly, and then only P_77 of the four published entries matches: P_66 is 0.4154 vs a published 0.6010, and P_76 is -0.1415 vs a published +0.0495 (claimed equal to Phi). The proof block's key lemma Delta_1 = 0 holds only when the target is strand 0, while the producer flips the last strand; and even under the block's own convention the chain yields -0.0467 rather than Phi = +0.0495. Blocks the convention-D migration of Phi, P_66 and P_67 -- P_77 is unaffected and stays derived.
caveats: NOT a claim that the published forms are wrong. The only recorded construction lives in a _deprecated file that neither the content blocks nor the live producer cite, so it may itself be superseded by a derivation absent from the tree. What is established: the two disagree on three of four entries, the proof block's key lemma is convention-dependent and false as the producer runs, and the corpus does not record which side is current. NOTE the universality result WEAKENS a transcription-drift reading: a structural claim (all three control pairs giving the same amplitude) cannot arise from a mistyped number. Universality is now measured under BOTH indexings and fails under both, including the target-first reading where the block's own key lemma Delta_1 = 0 does hold -- so no choice of convention rescues it. That removes one of the two branches this probe previously could not separate: the published trio does not come from this construction under any reading of it. It remains possible that a different, unrecorded derivation produces them; the probe still cannot speak to a derivation that is not in the tree.
